nc93b25d93ec.s: Which ruler of Kashmir checked the expansion of the Pratihara king Mihira Bhoja?
nc93b25d93ec.x: Mihira Bhoja's expansion was checked by Sankaravarman of Kashmir, along with the Rashtrakuta Krishna II and the Pala Devapala.

n6cadb2c1796.s: In which year did Mahmud of Ghazni attack Kannauj, hastening the decline of the Gurjara-Pratiharas?
n6cadb2c1796.x: Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Kannauj in 1018, one of the blows (with Indra III's raid and the secession of feudatories) that weakened Pratihara power.

n65648679683.s: Near which place did the Pratihara king Nagabhata II defeat the Pala ruler Dharmapala?
n65648679683.x: Nagabhata II ousted Chakrayudha, defeated Dharmapala near Monghyr and made Kannauj the Pratihara capital.

n316d3efc50f.s: The Arab merchant Sulaiman (mid-9th century) referred to Mihira Bhoja as:
n316d3efc50f.x: Sulaiman called Mihira Bhoja 'Juzr' or 'Al-Juzr'; 'Baura' was Al-Masudi's name for him and Adivaraha was Bhoja's own title on his coins.

nindian-history-21-8.s: Which ruler of Sindh was defeated and killed by Muhammad bin Qasim?
nindian-history-21-8.x: Muhammad bin Qasim led the Arab invasion of Sindh, defeated and killed Raja Dahir, and his conquest stayed largely within Sindh and Multan.

n813b56baa11.s: The Pratihara king Vatsaraja, after taking Kannauj and defeating Dharmapala, was defeated by which Rashtrakuta ruler?
n813b56baa11.x: Vatsaraja took Kannauj and defeated Dharmapala but was later defeated by the Rashtrakuta Dhruva, marking the beginning of the tripartite struggle.

n359ab708894.s: Kavirajamarga, the earliest work on Kannada poetics, is associated with which Rashtrakuta ruler?
n359ab708894.x: Kavirajamarga (c. 850) is associated with Amoghavarsha I and is the earliest work on Kannada poetics.

n284e76cab32.s: The Kannada poet Ponna was patronised by:
n284e76cab32.x: Ponna was patronised by the Rashtrakuta Krishna III; Pampa was patronised by Arikesari II and Ranna by Tailapa II.

ndbb2de0e165.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler is credited with fighting 108 battles against the Rashtrakuta forces?
ndbb2de0e165.x: Vijayaditya II of Vengi is credited with fighting 108 battles against the Rashtrakutas.

nf0d13245ba4.s: Pampa's Kannada epic Vikramarjuna Vijaya is also known as:
nf0d13245ba4.x: Vikramarjuna Vijaya is also called Pampa Bharata; in it Pampa modelled Arjuna on his patron Arikesari II.

n290b05a2e7f.s: After his victory at Vingavalli, the Rashtrakuta Amoghavarsha I assumed the title:
n290b05a2e7f.x: Amoghavarsha I won at Vingavalli and took the title Viranarayana.

nbb8735ee9ee.s: Manyakheta, the Rashtrakuta capital, was built by:
nbb8735ee9ee.x: Amoghavarsha I built Manyakheta; the early Rashtrakuta seat had been in the Elapura (Ellora) region.

na5b2e6b5fe9.s: The Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III defeated the Cholas at the Battle of:
na5b2e6b5fe9.x: Krishna III defeated the Cholas at Takkolam (949 CE).

n94ff060cb66.s: The first Rashtrakuta ruler to proceed towards northern India was:
n94ff060cb66.x: Dhruva was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to move north; he defeated Vatsaraja and Dharmapala.

ne4f5766496b.x: Jinasena wrote a Sanskrit Adipurana, while Pampa wrote a Kannada Adipurana on the life of Rishabhadeva.

nindian-history-17-18.s: Who led the Chola side at the Battle of Takkolam (949 CE)?
nindian-history-17-18.x: Rajaditya led the Cholas at Takkolam, where the Western Gangas and Vaidumbas fought on the Rashtrakuta side.

n20a15a30545.s: 'Nripatunga' was a title of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
n20a15a30545.x: Nripatunga and Viranarayana were titles of Amoghavarsha I; Prabhutavarsha was associated with Govinda III.

nefc9433b7ec.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rashtrakuta trade?
o: Horses were imported by sea from Arabia.
Arab merchants were barred from settling in the western ports.
Textiles were among the goods exported.
Cambay, Thana and Sopara were western ports connected with this trade.
nefc9433b7ec.x: Arab merchants settled peacefully in the western ports, so the statement that they were barred is false; the horse imports, textile exports and the listed ports are correct.

n3355a26535f.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora is which cave of the Ellora group?
n3355a26535f.x: The monolithic Kailasa temple is Cave 16; Cave 10 is the Buddhist chaitya.

n1c7ae444adc.s: The three-headed Shiva known as Trimurti or Maheshamurti is the principal masterpiece of:
n1c7ae444adc.x: The Trimurti (Maheshamurti) is the masterpiece of the Elephanta island caves near Mumbai, whose main cave many historians date to the sixth-century Kalachuris.

ncb801eb9e7b.s: The Arab traveller Al-Masudi visited the Rashtrakuta kingdom (c. 915-16 CE) during the reign of:
ncb801eb9e7b.x: Al-Masudi came c. 915-16 CE under Indra III and described the Balhara as having many Arab/Muslim subjects.

nb12d32ba71f.s: The Ellora caves are carved in which hills of Aurangabad district, Maharashtra?
nb12d32ba71f.x: Ellora lies in the Charanandri hills near the Elaganga river, on the ancient Ujjain-Deccan route; the caves were carved c. 600-1000 CE.

n608d643d8aa.s: In Rashtrakuta administration, the Vishaya was headed by the:
n608d643d8aa.x: The Vishaya was headed by the Vishayapati; the Rashtra by the Rashtrapati, the Bhukti by the Bhogapati and the Grama by the Gramakuta or gavunda.

n5c61112c762.s: The early Rashtrakuta rulers were staunch followers of:
n5c61112c762.x: Early Rashtrakuta rulers were staunch Shaivas, though Vaishnavism and Buddhism also received patronage without persecution.

ne25740aec80.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was carved during the reign of which Rashtrakuta ruler?
ne25740aec80.x: The Kailasa temple, with its three-tiered Dravida vimana, was carved under Krishna I (r. 756-773), not Dantidurga or Amoghavarsha.

nbf972414d8d.s: The Hindu caves (13-29) at Ellora are mainly the work of the:
nbf972414d8d.x: The Hindu caves at Ellora are mainly Rashtrakuta work; the Buddhist caves (c. 600-730 CE) are the earliest and the Jain caves the latest.

n66acc65be03.s:
Arrange the following Badami Chalukya rulers in chronological order:
1. Mangalesha
2. Pulakesin I
3. Vikramaditya I
4. Kirtivarman I
n66acc65be03.x: Pulakesin I founded the kingdom with Badami as capital, Kirtivarman I expanded it, Mangalesha then ruled as regent, and Vikramaditya I later restored Chalukya power after the Pallava occupation of Vatapi.

n64502f2e34d.s: According to the Aihole inscription, Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the banks of which river?
n64502f2e34d.x: The Aihole inscription says Pulakesin II defeated Harsha at the Narmada; it also records victories over Kosala, Kalinga and the Pallavas.

na4f16640bb8.s: In which year did Kubja Vishnuvardhana declare independence at Vengi, founding the Eastern Chalukya line?
na4f16640bb8.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana was appointed at Vengi in 617 CE after Pulakesin II's conquest and declared independence in 624 CE, with Pithapuram as capital.

nindian-history-144-2-2.s: Which Badami Chalukya ruler annexed the Kadambas, the Gangas and the Mauryas of Konkan?
nindian-history-144-2-2.x: Kirtivarman I annexed the Kadambas, Gangas and Mauryas of Konkan; Pulakesin I performed the Ashvamedha and Pulakesin II took the title Dakshinapatheshwara.

n7004cd5267e.s: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with which Persian king?
n7004cd5267e.x: Pulakesin II exchanged embassies with the Persian king Khusrau II; the Ajanta Cave 1 painting once read as this embassy is now doubted.

nebc98a59b94.s: Pulakesin II assumed the title Paramesvara after defeating:
nebc98a59b94.x: Pulakesin II took the title Paramesvara after defeating Harsha, not Mahendravarman I; his other titles included Dakshinapatheshwara, Satyashraya and Prithvivallabha.

n0d7a1efd335.s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II (634-35 CE) is engraved on which temple?
n0d7a1efd335.x: The Aihole prasasti by Ravikirti is on the Meguti Jain temple at Aihole; the Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Lokamahadevi.

nindian-history-144-2-5.s: Ravikirti, author of the Aihole inscription, compared his fame with that of:
nindian-history-144-2-5.x: Ravikirti names Kalidasa and Bharavi in the Aihole inscription, claiming to equal their fame.

nindian-history-144-2-9.s: Which Pallava king captured and destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda?
nindian-history-144-2-9.x: The Pallava Narasimhavarman I destroyed Vatapi in 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda; Chalukya power was later restored by Vikramaditya I.

nindian-history-144-2-24.s: The Aihole inscription, composed by Ravikirti, is written in which language?
nindian-history-144-2-24.x: The Aihole inscription is in Sanskrit (not Prakrit), in the Southern Brahmi script, and is the key source for Pulakeshin II.

n9ae3b63a27c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Badami Chalukya society and administration?
o: Agraharas were land grants made to Brahmins.
R.S. Sharma called their spread the 'proliferation of the feudal land grant system'.
Vatapi and Aihole had no urban or trade role.
n9ae3b63a27c.x: Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres, not purely religious ones, so that statement is false; the other three are correct.

nfce21d4255b.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Chalukya-Pallava conflict)?
o: Power that replaced the Badami Chalukyas – Cholas
Pallava occupation of Vatapi – about 13 years
Vikramaditya I – recovered Vatapi c. 655 CE
nfce21d4255b.x: The Chalukya-Pallava rivalry ended when the Rashtrakutas, not the Cholas, replaced the Chalukyas in the mid-eighth century; the other pairs are correct (642 to c. 655).

n7672b045a08.s: Vikramaditya II occupied Kanchi around 740 CE during the reign of which Pallava king?
n7672b045a08.x: Vikramaditya II entered Kanchi c. 740 CE in Nandivarman II's reign, gifted gold to the Rajasimheshvara temple and left a Kannada inscription on a pillar.

ncfc948ae760.s: Vijayabhattarika, who issued land grants in her own name, was the queen of:
ncfc948ae760.x: Vijayabhattarika (Vijaya-mahadevi) was the queen of Chandraditya; she governed and issued land grants in her own name.

n7873303308e.s: Which inscription, composed by Ravikirti, records the conflict between Pulakesin II and Harsha?
n7873303308e.x: The Aihole inscription by Ravikirti, together with Hiuen Tsang's account, is the source for the Pulakesin II-Harsha conflict; the Kailasanatha inscription is not.

nindian-history-144-2-15.s: Which Badami Chalukya queen administered the kingdom after the death of her husband Chandraditya?
nindian-history-144-2-15.x: Vijaya Bhattarika, queen of Chandraditya, governed after his death, reflecting how the Badami Chalukyas often gave women high administrative posts.

n2bc6010e857.s: In the first round of the Chalukya-Pallava conflict, Pulakesin II advanced up to:
n2bc6010e857.x: In the first round Pulakesin II advanced to Kanchi and won territory in the Krishna-Godavari region; in the second round Narasimhavarman I defeated him and took Vatapi.

ne2e55849814.s: The Renati Chodas of Rayalaseema were first feudatories of the early Pallavas and later of the:
ne2e55849814.x: The Renati Chodas were initially feudatories of the early Pallavas and subsequently of the Badami Chalukyas.

na4897fd95bd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the temples at Pattadakal?
o: The Virupaksha temple was built by Queen Lokamahadevi to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.
The Mallikarjuna temple was built by Queen Trailokyamahadevi in the Dravida style.
The Virupaksha temple is modelled on the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi.
The Papanatha temple is built in the Dravida style.
na4897fd95bd.x: The Papanatha temple (like Kashi Vishwanatha) is in the Nagara style, not Dravida; the other three statements are correct.

nce748586bd4.s: Which of the four main Badami cave temples is a Jain cave?
nce748586bd4.x: Badami has four principal sandstone caves of the 6th-7th centuries, the earliest made under Mangalesha; the fourth cave is Jain.

na7eba33215d.s: The Navabrahma temples of the Badami Chalukyas at Alampur stand on the banks of which river?
na7eba33215d.x: The Navabrahma group is a complex of nine Nagara temples on the Tungabhadra at Alampur, built by the Badami Chalukyas in the 7th-8th centuries.

n5515b6529e6.s: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal copies the tradition of which temple?
n5515b6529e6.x: The Dravida-style Virupaksha temple copies the Pallava Kailasanatha tradition of Kanchi, a line continued by the Rashtrakuta Kailasa at Ellora.

n87111d7cf33.s: Which temple at Aihole has the earliest massive bracket capital?
n87111d7cf33.x: The Lad Khan temple, rectangular with a flat roof and stone grilles (and no shikhara), has the earliest massive bracket capital.

n71c272e9ec2.s: The narrative friezes at Pattadakal depict scenes from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the:
n71c272e9ec2.x: Pattadakal is noted for narrative friezes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Panchatantra, along with Nandi mandapas and polished pillars.

ne918aab4483.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
ne918aab4483.s: The Prakrit Mayidavolu plates, among the earliest Pallava records, were issued as yuvaraja by:
ne918aab4483.x: The Mayidavolu plates were issued by Sivaskandavarman as yuvaraja; the Manchikallu inscription belongs to the Pallava Simhavarman.

nf81881c37c0.s: Which dynasty pioneered Dravida temple art in South India?
nf81881c37c0.x: The Pallavas pioneered Dravida temple art; under them the Grantha script spread and the Alvar-Nayanar Bhakti movement grew.

n9612b7f978a.s: Which Pallava ruler built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi?
n9612b7f978a.x: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla, an ardent Vaishnavite and contemporary of Tirumangai Alvar, built the Vaikuntha Perumal temple at Kanchi.

n63e9924a04d.s: The Pallava king Mahendravarman I was converted from Jainism to Shaivism by:
n63e9924a04d.x: Mahendravarman I began as a Jain and was converted to Shaivism by Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), not Sambandar.

n2c1d140f120.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Undavalli caves?
o: They are located in Guntur district on the banks of the Krishna.
They were built by the Cholas.
They contain a monolithic reclining Anantasayana Vishnu.
n2c1d140f120.x: Undavalli is a Vishnukundin complex, not a Chola work; the location, multi-storeyed form and reclining Anantasayana Vishnu are correct.

nbd1c1f60796.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
nbd1c1f60796.s: Bhairavakonda, whose eight caves resemble early Pallava caves, was a centre of:
nbd1c1f60796.x: Bhairavakonda, with eight caves resembling early Pallava caves, was a centre of Shaivism, not Jainism.

n5adcbfe4d54.s: The Jain cave of Sittannavasal, with murals of a lotus pond, is in which district of Tamil Nadu?
n5adcbfe4d54.x: Sittannavasal is a Jain cave in Pudukkottai; once credited to Mahendravarman I, an inscription records a 9th-century Pandya renovation.

n8e03b12aa98.s: Each of the Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram was carved out of a single rock of:
n8e03b12aa98.x: The Pancha Rathas are monolithic, each carved from a single granite rock, imitating earlier wooden and structural forms.

nceee4abd48f.s: Which is the largest ratha at Mahabalipuram and a precursor of the Dravida vimana?
nceee4abd48f.x: The Dharmaraja ratha is the largest and a precursor of the Dravida vimana; the Draupadi ratha is the smallest, a hut-shaped single cell.

n9ee025f6082.s: Besides two Shiva shrines, the structural Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram contains a shrine of:
n9ee025f6082.x: The Shore Temple is a structural temple with two Shiva shrines and one Vishnu shrine, the surviving temple of the Seven Pagodas tradition.

n5cc2e2ea1f9.s: The Mandagapattu inscription, describing a temple made without brick, timber, metal or mortar, was issued by:
n5cc2e2ea1f9.x: The Mandagapattu inscription of Mahendravarman I (not Narasimhavarman I) records a temple for Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva made without brick, timber, metal or mortar.

n1a02d3fb47f.s: The construction of the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi was completed by:
n1a02d3fb47f.x: The Kailasanatha temple, rich in Shiva sculptures and a model for later Chola temples, was completed by Mahendravarman III.

nindian-history-145-18.s:
Assertion (A): The Eastern Chalukyas originated as a branch of the Badami Chalukyas.
Reason (R): Kubja Vishnuvardhana, the first Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi, was the brother of Pulakeshin II.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nindian-history-145-18.x: Both are true: the Eastern Chalukyas branched from the Badami line because Kubja Vishnuvardhana, Pulakeshin II's brother, founded their rule in Vengi.

n27681025661.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Vengi school of Eastern Chalukya architecture)?
o: Name of the style – Vesara or Chalukya
Vimana – Dravidian form with Buddhist influence
Base of the temple – raised jagati
n27681025661.x: The Vengi school used local sandstone, not granite; the Vesara/Chalukya name, Dravidian vimana with Buddhist influence and raised jagati are correct.

n4d960d236af.s: The Nandampudi inscription, recording Rajaraja Narendra's grant to Narayana Bhattu, was written by:
n4d960d236af.x: The Nandampudi inscription of Rajaraja Narendra, recording his grant to Narayana Bhattu, was written by Nannaya.

n801f8d8c029.s: 'Rajamartanda' was a title of which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
n801f8d8c029.x: Vimaladitya bore the title Rajamartanda; Chalukya Bhima was Kollabhiganda, Saktivarma I Chalukya Chandra and Rajaraja Narendra Rajarajanarayana.

n5d8b2f318a1.s: Which Eastern Chalukya ruler made Rajamahendravaram (Rajahmundry) his capital?
n5d8b2f318a1.x: Ammaraja I made Rajamahendravaram his capital, and Rajaraja Narendra later ruled from it and made it famous; Jayasimha Vallabha I had shifted the capital to Vengi.

n294e87c9799.s: According to the Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva, Chalukya Bhima I fought how many battles?
n294e87c9799.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Mallappadeva credits Chalukya Bhima I, who ruled 30 years and built the Pancharamas, with 360 battles.

nf6da8b57812.s: The Rashtrakuta Dhruva, after defeating Vishnuvardhana IV, married his daughter:
nf6da8b57812.x: Vishnuvardhana IV, who backed Govinda III, was defeated by Dhruva, who then married his daughter Sheela Mahadevi.

n154d49fe97d.s: In which year was the Eastern Chalukya ruler Rajaraja Narendra crowned?
n154d49fe97d.x: Rajaraja Narendra was crowned in 1022 CE; Saktivarman I defeated Satyasraya in 1006 CE and Vijayaditya VII was ousted in 1070 CE.

nb3e0fbe5e86.x: Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara was Narayana Bhattu's title; Nannaya was known as Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu.

nae7b0f5d14a.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (religion under the Eastern Chalukyas)?
o: Vimaladitya – only Vengi Chalukya king to become a Jain
Amaravati – centre where declining Buddhism survived
Family of Basaveshwara – Jains who migrated to Karnataka
nae7b0f5d14a.x: Potlacheruvu was a famous Jain centre, not a Buddhist one; the other three pairs are correct.

n31bd9bfab47.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
n31bd9bfab47.s: The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu took place during the:
n31bd9bfab47.x: The persecution of Jains at Potlacheruvu occurred in the Kakatiya age, not under the Eastern Chalukyas, who patronised Jainism, Buddhism and Hinduism.

n7e6334345cb.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, Chellavva is an example of a:
n7e6334345cb.x: Musicians and dancers were attached to Eastern Chalukya temples and courts, and Chellavva is an example of such a court-linked singer and dancer.

n319a6b718a7.s: 'Kavigayaka Kalpataru' was the title of which Eastern Chalukya ruler?
n319a6b718a7.x: Ammaraja II was Kavigayaka Kalpataru; Vishnuvardhana III was Kavi Pandita Kamadhenu and Rajaraja Narendra Kavyageetha Priyudu.

n148f26275b8.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the council of ministers was called:
n148f26275b8.x: The Eastern Chalukya council of ministers was called Tirthulu, and the Samaharta was its chief member.

n19f08161ede.s: The dispatch of 72 merchants to China is associated with:
n19f08161ede.x: The 72-merchant mission to China is associated with Kulothunga I; Saktivarma's coins have been found in Arakan, Burma.

n2c40dc6d600.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 108 Shiva temples of the Eastern Chalukyas?
o: They were built by Vijayaditya II (Narendramrigaraja).
They were called Narendresvaralayas or Narendra Mrigeswaralayas.
One temple was built at each of his 108 battle sites.
The source for this claim is the Kopparam inscription.
n2c40dc6d600.x: The source is the Sataluru inscription; the Kopparam inscription is Pulakesin II's record. The other three statements are correct.

n3a18ceadcc2.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
n3a18ceadcc2.s: Eastern Chalukya temple building was concentrated in the:
n3a18ceadcc2.x: Eastern Chalukya (Vengi school, Vesara/Chalukya style) temple building was concentrated in the Krishna-Godavari delta.

nab1f4c0d3cc.s: The Bikkavolu (Biccavolu) temple group belongs to the time of:
nab1f4c0d3cc.x: The Bikkavolu group belongs to Gunaga Vijayaditya's time (9th century); Chalukya Bhima I built the Bhimeswara temples at Draksharama and Samalkot.

n4a177e6921d.s: Ksheerarama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
n4a177e6921d.x: Ksheerarama is at Palakollu (West Godavari); Kumararama is at Samalkot, Amararama at Amaravati and Draksharama at Draksharama.

n9166283126a.s: Which of the Pancharama temples is NOT two-storeyed?
n9166283126a.x: All the Pancharamas except Ksheerarama are two-storeyed; the Skanda Purana and Srinatha's Bhimeswara Puranam are literary sources on them.

n7a8e2c25644.s: The two-storeyed Bhimeswara shrines at Draksharama and Samalkot were built by:
n7a8e2c25644.x: Both are two-storeyed Bhimeswara shrines of Chalukya Bhima I, later renovated by the Reddis; the Samalkot gopuram is a later addition.

n61d703b0197.s: Which temple at Rajahmundry later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs?
n61d703b0197.x: The Vishnu temple at Rajahmundry, linked with Rajaraja Narendra like the Kotilingala and Markandeya temples, later became the Pedda Masjid under the Tughlaqs.

ndd57a192038.s: Somarama, one of the Pancharamas, is located at:
ndd57a192038.x: Somarama is at Gunupudi near Bhimavaram; Samalkot is Bheemarama/Kumararama (Chalukya Bhimavaram) and Palakollu is Ksheerarama.

ne91301fd9b2.shape: one-liner (match not possible from the given facts)
ne91301fd9b2.s: Between 575 and 848 CE, Telugu appeared in full prose sentences in the records of which dynasty?
ne91301fd9b2.x: The Renati Cholas made Telugu a royal and legislative language, replacing Prakrit and Sanskrit, and from 575 to 848 CE Telugu appeared in full prose sentences.

nb26b1987eea.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
nb26b1987eea.s: Kavi-Brahma Tikkana was minister and court poet to:
nb26b1987eea.x: Tikkana was minister and court poet of Manumasiddhi II and sought Kakatiya Ganapati's help against Vijayaganda Gopala.

n949b3d353c0.s: The Nellore Chodas were associated with:
n949b3d353c0.x: The Nellore Chodas were associated with Vikrama Simhapuri; the Konidena Chodas with Kammanadu, the Pottapi Chodas with Pottapi (Kadapa) and the Renati Chodas with Renadu.

na95d518cbb9.s: The Renati Cholas gave Telugu its first royal dignity approximately how many centuries before Nannaya?
na95d518cbb9.x: By using Telugu in royal and legislative records, the Renati Cholas gave it royal dignity about five centuries before Nannaya.

nd0cc73b03ef.s: How many Telugu inscriptions of the Renati Cholas, mostly donation records, are known?
nd0cc73b03ef.x: Thirty-three Renati Chola Telugu inscriptions are known, most of them donation records (dana sasanalu).

n959a1c4a914.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about political succession in Coastal Andhra?
o: The Kakatiyas succeeded the Velanati Chodas.
The Eastern Chalukyas preceded the Velanati Chodas.
The Qutb Shahis came after 1565 in the later succession.
n959a1c4a914.x: The Reddis succeeded the Kakatiyas, not the other way round; the other three statements are correct.

n3b3f269f7e0.s: After the Musunuri period, Prolaya Vemareddy is associated with which political formation?
n3b3f269f7e0.x: Prolaya Vemareddy is associated with the Reddis; Singama with the Velamas, Harihara-Bukka with Vijayanagara and Hasan Gangu with the Bahmanis.

ne8be5ff2d8f.s: In which year was the Battle of Muttukur fought?
ne8be5ff2d8f.x: Muttukur was fought in 1263; Raichur in 1520, Rakshasi-Tangadi on 26 January 1565 and Palnadu in the 12th century.

ne455b203ac2.s: The Raichur Doab (Raichur Antarvedi), the main cause of the Bahmani-Vijayanagara wars, lies between which rivers?
ne455b203ac2.x: The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra; the Krishna-Godavari doab was a separate coastal contest.

n4f62d5a3a09.s: Who was the last ruler of the Qutb Shahi state?
n4f62d5a3a09.x: The Shia, Persian-using Qutb Shahi state ended under Abul Hasan Tana Shah.

nap-history-16-8.s: Who founded the Ikshvaku dynasty of the Krishna valley?
nap-history-16-8.x: Shantamula I founded the Ikshvaku dynasty; Simuka founded the Satavahana dynasty.

n52753c86ad4.s: Which Vijayanagara leader was killed in the Battle of Rakshasi-Tangadi (Talikota)?
n52753c86ad4.x: Aliya Rama Raya was killed at Rakshasi-Tangadi (also called Talikota or Bannihatti), fought against Golconda, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Bidar.

n76300cbf19e.s: In which year did the Delhi Sultanate replace the Kakatiyas at Warangal?
n76300cbf19e.x: The Telangana succession ran Kakatiyas, Delhi Sultanate (1323), Musunuri Nayakas, Velamas/Bahmanis and then the Qutb Shahis.

nc12dbbc9d11.s: Which dynasty is regarded as the second unifier of all Telugu lands?
nc12dbbc9d11.x: The Satavahanas, Kakatiyas and Qutb Shahis are regarded as the first, second and third unifiers of the Telugu lands.

n37be452eeab.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the figures of the Palnadu war?
o: Nagamma was a Shaivite minister on Nalagamaraju's side.
Nagamma built the Veerabhadra Swamy temple at Gurajala.
n37be452eeab.x: Brahmanaidu led the Malideva faction; Nagamma was on Nalagamaraju's side and opposed his reforms.

n2ee68e06888.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched (Velanati Chodas)?
o: Areas included – Bapatla, Tenali, Repalle and Guntur
n2ee68e06888.x: Mallavarma was the progenitor of the Velanati Chodas and Gonka I was the founder, so 'Founder – Mallavarma' is wrong.

ncbe3205a9e8.s: The Kalingattuparani, describing Kulottunga I's conquest of Kalinga by sea, was written by:
ncbe3205a9e8.x: Jayangondar's Kalingattuparani describes Kulottunga I's maritime conquest of Kalinga; Kulottunga I also sent 72 merchants to China and built Kulottunga Cholapuram.

nc2f12f3bed3.s: The Gona Haihayas were associated with:
nc2f12f3bed3.x: The Gona Haihayas were associated with Vardhamanapuram; the Palnadu Haihayas with Gurajala and the Panchadhara Haihayas with the Visakhapatnam-Yelamanchili region.

n7b08d7e11ae.s: In post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra, the vassals of the nadus accepted the overlordship first of Velanadu and later of the:
n7b08d7e11ae.x: Post-Eastern Chalukya Andhra was a web of nadus under vassals, who accepted Velanadu and later Kakatiya overlordship when those powers were strong.

n3daa1a1e966.s: The Velanati Choda line ended when its last member was killed by the Kakatiya ruler:
n3daa1a1e966.x: The Velanati line ended when Kakatiya Ganapatideva killed its last member (named in some sources as Prithvisvara).

nd48807918e0.s: In which year did Kulottunga I take the Chola throne?
nd48807918e0.x: Kulottunga I took the Chola throne in 1070 and Vengi in 1075, after the death of Vijayaditya VII, the last Eastern Chalukya.

nindian-history-37-17.s: Parashar Madhav, a commentary on the Parashara Smriti, was written by:
nindian-history-37-17.x: Parashar Madhav is Madhavacharya's commentary on the Parashara Smriti; Mitakshara is Vijnanesvara's and Chaturvarga Chintamani is Hemadri's.

n2f4acf74eed.s: The Kalyani Chalukya Someshvara I granted Hanamkonda to which Kakatiya chief?
n2f4acf74eed.x: Someshvara I granted Hanamkonda to Kakatiya Prola I; he also killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam and took the title Vengi Purveshwara.

n6e63cfc7271.s: The 100-chapter Sanskrit encyclopaedia Manasollasa is also called:
n6e63cfc7271.x: Manasollasa, also called Abhilashitartha Chintamani, covers statecraft, agriculture, medicine, astronomy, music, dance and cuisine.

nb3942ab2297.s: The Kalyani Chalukya dynasty came to an end around:
nb3942ab2297.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas ended around 1189 CE, and the Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Yadavas emerged as successor powers.

nb75669c2c27.s: Kalyani Chalukya temples in the mature Vesara (Gadag) style were built mainly of:
nb75669c2c27.x: The Kalyani Chalukyas built mainly in chloritic schist (soapstone), not granite; their stellate plans later became a model for the Hoysalas.

n91e96cbcbf2.x: Jimutavahana wrote the Dayabhaga; Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara and Hemadri the Chaturvarga Chintamani.

n5225e95e6dd.s: After the weakening of the Kalyani Chalukyas, the Yadavas (Seunas) ruled from:
n5225e95e6dd.x: The Yadavas or Seunas ruled from Devagiri; the Hoysalas from Dwarasamudra, the Kakatiyas from Hanamkonda-Warangal and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.

n64e44c30fa5.s: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara at the court of:
n64e44c30fa5.x: Vijnaneshwara wrote the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, at the court of Vikramaditya VI.

n7efd941f251.s: The Mahadeva temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period is located at:
n7efd941f251.x: The Mahadeva temple is at Itagi; Kasivishveshvara is at Lakkundi, Doddabasappa at Dambal and Kedareshwara at Balligavi.

nindian-history-37-15.s: The legal digest Smriti Chandrika was written by:
nindian-history-37-15.x: Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika; Hemadri compiled Chaturvarga Chintamani and Ballal Sena wrote Daan Sagar.

nindian-history-37-14.s: The Mitakshara is based on which Smriti?
nindian-history-37-14.x: The Yajnavalkya Smriti is the basis of the Mitakshara; the Manusmriti is ascribed to Manu.

nf8e27aae2b7.s: Which of the following Kalyani Chalukya rulers came earliest?
nf8e27aae2b7.x: Tailapa II preceded Satyasraya, who was followed by Someshvara I and later Vikramaditya VI.

n4d064794254.s: Under the Dayabhaga system, sons acquire a right in ancestral property:
n4d064794254.x: Dayabhaga recognises the sons' right in ancestral property only after the father's death, whereas Mitakshara gives it by birth.

n6b64082c730.s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler bore the title Tribhuvanamalla and ruled for 50 years?
n6b64082c730.x: Vikramaditya VI, the greatest Kalyani Chalukya ruler, ruled for 50 years as Tribhuvanamalla and brought the Vengi feudatories under his control.

na256b294e3c.s: 'Ulakalanda Perumal', a title reflecting a land survey and revenue reorganisation, belonged to:
na256b294e3c.x: Ulakalanda Perumal and Mummudi Chola were titles of Rajaraja I; Madurai-konda was Parantaka I's and Gangaikonda Chola Rajendra I's.

ncbb481b8378.s: Which Chola ruler placed Saktivarman and Vimaladitya as Eastern Chalukya princes in Vengi?
ncbb481b8378.x: Rajaraja I arranged Vengi by placing Saktivarman and Vimaladitya there; he also captured Quilon, annexed Madurai and conquered the Maldives.

n87f0cad7a6d.s: The Battle of Kudalasangamam was won by the Cholas under:
n87f0cad7a6d.x: Virarajendra won at Kudalasangamam; Krishna III's Rashtrakutas won Takkolam and Rajendra I's army won at Kalidindi.

n26ddfb74dd2.s: Which historian said the Cholas turned the Bay of Bengal into a 'Chola Lake'?
n26ddfb74dd2.x: K.A. Nilakanta Sastri described the Bay of Bengal as a 'Chola Lake'; the 1025 CE Srivijaya expedition was led by Rajendra I.

n5adb8a1512e.s: In May 2026, the Netherlands returned which Chola copper plates to India at The Hague?
n5adb8a1512e.x: The Anaimangalam (Leiden) plates, ordered by Rajaraja I and engraved under Rajendra I, were returned on 16 May 2026 during the PM's visit.

n9d78d045f1b.s: Chola overseas naval activity helped spread which art tradition to Southeast Asia?
n9d78d045f1b.x: The Cholas, described as the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, helped spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia.

n61dc487657c.s: Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I) was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and:
n61dc487657c.x: Kulottunga I, also called Rajendra Chalukya, was the son of Rajaraja Narendra and Ammanga Devi and took the Chola throne in 1070 CE.

n8334240eb0b.s: Which ruler united the Tamil (Chola) and Andhra (Vengi) kingdoms?
n8334240eb0b.x: Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms; Vengi had been a prize in the Chola-Chalukya wars, and the Mandalika Yugam followed (1076 to c. 1210).

nindian-history-148-7.x: Gangaikondacholapuram was built by Rajendra I; his father Rajaraja I took northern Sri Lanka, conquered the Maldives and built a navy.

n7afba60559d.s: The Chola king Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) was also known as:
n7afba60559d.x: Rajaraja I, also known as Arumolivarman, ruled 985-1014 CE and made the Chola state the largest in South India.

n00802edf164.x: 'Coromandel' comes from Cholamandalam, not Tondaimandalam (the former Pallava country); the Chola core was the Kaveri delta.

nindian-history-148-3.s: Which Sri Lankan king was defeated and captured by Rajendra I when he completed the Chola conquest of Ceylon?
nindian-history-148-3.x: Rajendra I completed the conquest of Ceylon by taking its southern part and capturing Mahinda V, building on Rajaraja I's conquest of the north.

nindian-history-148-11.s: The Chola king Kulottunga I (1070-1122 CE) is noted for abolishing:
nindian-history-148-11.x: Kulottunga I abolished tolls and married his daughter to a Sinhala prince; the Brihadeeswara temple was built by Rajaraja I.

nea08a530092.s: Which Chola king defeated the Sailendra ruler at Kadaram in the 1025 CE expedition?
nea08a530092.x: Rajendra I defeated the Sailendra ruler at Kadaram in 1025 CE; Rajaraja I built the Brihadeshvara temple, conducted a land survey and captured the Maldives.

n9803a9f50bb.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
n9803a9f50bb.s: Which of the following South Indian polities is described as highly centralised?
n9803a9f50bb.x: The Badami Chalukya polity is described as highly centralised, whereas Pallava, Chola and Rashtrakuta records show active local and village assemblies.

nc45b40dbd47.s: Under the Uttaramerur system, a candidate for a Chola village committee had to own at least:
nc45b40dbd47.x: Qualifications included owning at least 1/4 veli of land, an own house, age 35-70 and Vedic knowledge; recent committee service was a disqualification.

n8cafb30bfd3.s: Under the 73rd Amendment, the intermediate tier of Panchayats may be omitted in a State whose population does not exceed:
n8cafb30bfd3.x: The intermediate tier is optional in a State with a population not exceeding twenty lakh; Panchayats have five-year terms and elections follow dissolution within six months.

n10b1d4082d4.s: Chola village assemblies collected royal dues:
n10b1d4082d4.x: Royal dues were collected in cash, kind or both; the assembly also owned village lands, raised loans, levied taxes and auctioned defaulters' land.

n040482b3e6e.s: Participation in Chola sabhas was associated with:
n040482b3e6e.x: Sabha participation was tied to propertied, Vedic-learned Brahmins, so the system is criticised as elitist; it was not based on universal adult franchise.

nd86bfa87717.s: Which Article of the Constitution reserves not less than one-third of Panchayat seats for women?
nd86bfa87717.x: Article 243D reserves one-third of Panchayat seats and chairperson posts for women, unlike the Chola village assemblies, which had no quota for women.

n603385cc41b.s: In the Chola period, the nattar was the assembly of:
o: merchants of the nadu's market town
Brahmin landholders of a single village
leading vellala landholders of the nadu
n603385cc41b.x: The nattar was the nadu assembly of leading vellala landholders, handling revenue and disputes above village level; the merchant body was the nagaram.

ne9abfbec70e.s: In Chola village administration, the term 'kudumbu' meant:
ne9abfbec70e.x: Kudumbu meant ward; perumakkal meant assembly members, variyapperumakkal elected committee members, and variyam the committee system.

nf76254a4e8a.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions (919 and 921 CE) belong to which Chola ruler?
nf76254a4e8a.x: The two Uttaramerur inscriptions are of Parantaka I, dated 919 and 921 CE; Uttaramerur is in Kanchipuram district.

nindian-history-148-5.s: In Chola administration, the 'Nagaram' denoted the assembly of:
nindian-history-148-5.x: Nagaram was the body of merchant towns; Ur was the ordinary village assembly, Sabha the Brahmana village assembly, and Variyams were village committees.

naa3dfd4f65c.s: The lottery system used to select members of the Chola village assembly from among qualified persons was called:
naa3dfd4f65c.x: The Cholas used the kudavolai lottery among qualified persons, whereas Panchayat members under the 73rd Amendment are directly elected.

nindian-history-148-12.s: The unusually rich record of Chola history comes largely from extensive inscriptions engraved on:
nindian-history-148-12.x: The Cholas engraved long inscriptions on temple walls, which give an unusually rich record of their history.

n230c9ebe8bc.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP)?
o: Its first phase ran from 2016 to 2026.
The DILRMP 3.0 operational guidelines were issued by the Ministry of Rural Development.
DILRMP 3.0 covers survey/resurvey, ULPIN and cadastral maps.
n230c9ebe8bc.x: The first phase ran from 2008 to 2016; 2016-26 was the second phase, which brought ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar). The other statements are correct.

nb70275f2d8d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Chola officials and departments?
o: Puravu-varitinaikkalam or Shrikaranam was the revenue department.
Dharmasana was the royal court of justice.
nb70275f2d8d.x: Sirudaram denoted the lower officials; it was Perundaram that denoted the highest officials. The other statements are correct.

neb70240d1d2.s: Which of the following pairs (Chola fiscal and labour terms) is correctly matched?
o: Kasu – rural tax collected in cash
neb70240d1d2.x: Nettal denoted compulsory labour; Antarayam was a rural tax collected in cash, Eccoru the obligation to feed state officials and Kasu a gold coin.

nc887842001c.s: Which of the following pairs of Chola land terms is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Vellanvagai – land of non-Brahmin peasant proprietors
Salabhoga – land for maintaining a school
nc887842001c.x: Pallichchandam was land donated to Jaina institutions; land gifted to temples was devadana.

n0db6359050e.s: The Larger Leiden (Anaimangalam) plates record a grant to the Chulamanivarma-vihara built by the king of:
n0db6359050e.x: The plates, ordered by Rajaraja I and engraved under Rajendra I, grant Anaimangalam village to the vihara built by the Srivijaya king Sri Mara Vijayotunga Varman; they use Sanskrit and Tamil.

n0bac377a691.s: Chola inscriptions praised the king as a warrior, a patron of the arts and the protector of:
n0bac377a691.x: Chola kings were compared to gods, their images were installed beside deities, and inscriptions praised them as warriors, patrons of art and protectors of varnashrama dharma.

n514b48ccc7c.s: How many Mandalams (provinces) did the Chola Empire have?
n514b48ccc7c.x: The Chola Empire had eight Mandalams, each under a viceroy or governor who could be a prince or noble.

nd71a258cab5.s: In the Chola period, 'eripatti' was land whose revenue was set apart for the maintenance of:
nd71a258cab5.x: Eripatti revenue maintained the village tank; ghatikas were colleges attached to temples, and land gifted to temples was devadana.

nc36882a2871.s: Besides being landholders, employers and lenders, Chola temples served as venues for meetings of the:
nc36882a2871.x: Chola temples were major landholders, employers and lenders, and also provided venues for village assembly meetings.

ndb270863d3f.x: Karanmai was the right to cultivate and mitachi the superior possessory right; ulukudi were tenants and kaniyudaiyar the land-owning farmers.

n9df52c43713.s: In the Eastern Chalukya administration of Vengi, the Ashtadasha Tirthas were:
n9df52c43713.x: The Ashtadasha Tirthas were the 18 departments; the Yuvaraja was a partner in governance and councils were called Varagoshti.

n4ded58ba811.s: Rajendra I's 1025 CE expedition against Srivijaya captured Kadaram, identified with:
n4ded58ba811.x: Rajendra I's Srivijaya expedition took Kadaram (Kedah) in Malaya and parts of Sumatra.

nc80b00f6b9c.s: Burton Stein described the Chola state as a:
nc80b00f6b9c.x: Burton Stein used the concept of a segmentary state, while K.A. Nilakanta Sastri presented a more centralised picture.

n2649f5c95b2.s: Chola provincial territories that were not annexed but paid tribute were known as:
n2649f5c95b2.x: Chola provincial territories included annexed principalities and samanta or vassal territories that paid tribute.

n7a16deab8a1.s: Which merchant guild originated from Aihole and operated pan-regionally and overseas?
n7a16deab8a1.x: Ayyavole-500 originated from Aihole; Manigramam was a foreign-trade corporation, Ubhaya Nanadesi handled domestic and foreign trade, and Nagaram was a market-town assembly.

n73ff056058f.s: The 1088 Tamil inscription of the Ayyavole-500 merchant guild was found at:
n73ff056058f.x: Barus (Lobu Tua) has the 1088 Ayyavole-500 inscription; Takua Pa names Manigramam and Pagan has a Nanadesi Vishnu temple inscription.

nafe62207f22.s: As Chola power declined, the independence of the merchant guilds:
nafe62207f22.x: Merchant guilds, which had emblems and militias, acted as bankers and donated to temples, became more independent as the Cholas declined.

n4dea105bbf7.s: Under the Eastern Chalukyas, the Nakaras (merchant bodies) were headed by:
n4dea105bbf7.x: Nakaras headed by Shreshthis traded under the Eastern Chalukyas, and Ayyavole and Manigramam were active in Andhra, especially around Penugonda.

nindian-history-148-8.s: Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam of the Chola age were:
nindian-history-148-8.x: Ayyavole 500 and Manigramam were merchant guilds of the Chola age, part of a sea trade running from Sri Lanka through Malaya and Sumatra to Southeast Asia.

nfed07bd99ca.s: The 'Musical Steps' and the horse-drawn stone chariot are features of which Chola temple?
nfed07bd99ca.x: The Musical Steps and stone chariot belong to the Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, built by Rajaraja II; Kulottunga III built the Kampaharesvara at Tribhuvanam.

n0cf15ba78d3.s: The early friendly relations between the Cholas and Srivijaya are associated with the vihara at:
n0cf15ba78d3.x: Chola-Srivijaya relations began amicably, as seen in the Nagapattinam vihara, until obstruction of Indian traders led to Rajendra I's 1025 expedition to Kadaram.

n98f4120094d.s: In the Nataraja image, the damaru held in the upper right hand symbolises:
n98f4120094d.x: The damaru symbolises creation, the agni in the upper left hand destruction, and the prabhamandala the cosmic cycle; Apasmara represents ignorance.

n201bcc12262.s: The Nagara style of temple architecture is associated with a:
n201bcc12262.x: The Nagara temple has a curvilinear shikhara, while the Dravida temple has a pyramidal vimana and elaborate prakara walls and gateways.

n31bef3d93a6.s: Chola temples represent the zenith of which temple style?
n31bef3d93a6.x: Chola free-standing structural temples are the zenith of the Dravida style, not Nagara; the style continued under the Kalyani Chalukyas and Hoysalas.

nff4a150d2d8.s: The Chola-period cave paintings at Narthamalai depict:
nff4a150d2d8.x: Narthamalai paintings show Shiva and Parvati; Chola murals are also known at Gangaikondacholapuram, with fine Dakshinamurthy panels at Thanjavur.

nba1ffb2b1b8.s: In temple architecture, the 'antarala' is the:
o: vestibule between the sanctum and the mandapa
nba1ffb2b1b8.x: The antarala is the vestibule between sanctum and mandapa; the mandapa is a pillared hall, the jagati a raised platform and the gopuram the entrance gateway.

nd7e0f4d5600.s: The Saiva canon Tirumurai was compiled in the time of Rajaraja I by:
nd7e0f4d5600.x: Nambi Andar Nambi compiled the Tirumurai, the 12-book Saiva canon of Nayanar hymns (Periya Puranam the 12th); it does not include the Vaishnava Alvar hymns.

n419ff396a45.s: The Vesara style of temple architecture was pioneered by the:
n419ff396a45.x: Vesara, blending Dravida vimana tiers with the Nagara curvilinear profile, was pioneered by the Badami Chalukyas; the Hoysalas came later.

n71fe49792fb.s: The Tamil grammar Nannul was written by:
n71fe49792fb.x: Nannul is by Pavanandhi; Kalingattupparani is by Jayamkondar, Moovar Ula by Ottakuthar and Nalavenba by Pugalendi.

nf050c3e05bb.s: In the Chola Nataraja bronze, the lower right hand in abhaya mudra signifies:
nf050c3e05bb.x: Abhaya mudra means 'fear not', i.e. protection; the standard Nataraja is four-armed and the lower left hand points to the raised left foot.

na35b368fd35.s: The granite vimana of the Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur is about how high?
na35b368fd35.x: The vimana is about 216 feet high with a monolithic capstone of about 80 tonnes, and is built of granite, not brick.

nindian-history-148-4.s: The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram was built by:
nindian-history-148-4.x: Rajaraja II built the Airavatesvara temple; Rajaraja I built Brihadeeswara, Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram and Kulottunga I abolished tolls.

na6fedd2680c.s: The man's earring in the right ear and the woman's earring in the left ear of the Chola Nataraja symbolise:
o: the fusion of male and female principles
na6fedd2680c.x: The different earrings of the Nataraja image represent the fusion of male and female principles.

nfc70ae07524.s: Which of the following temple sites is NOT part of the UNESCO group 'Great Living Chola Temples'?
nfc70ae07524.x: The group comprises the temples at Thanjavur, Gangaikondacholapuram and Darasuram; Chidambaram is not included.

nindian-history-149-7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Hoysalas?
o: Belur was the earlier Hoysala capital.
Dwarasamudra (Halebidu) was the later Hoysala capital.
The Hoysaleshwara temple at Halebidu is dedicated to Vishnu.
The Chennakeshava temple was built by Vishnuvardhana.
nindian-history-149-7.x: The Hoysaleshwara at Halebidu is a Shiva temple, so that statement is false; the other three are correct.

n798836854b7.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates given)
n798836854b7.s: The Madanika (Salabhanjika) bracket figures are especially associated with which Hoysala temple site?
n798836854b7.x: The Madanika bracket figures are associated with Belur, not Somanathapura.

n7b93603b0c9.s: Hoysala temples with stellate plans were built on a raised platform of about one metre called the:
n7b93603b0c9.x: Hoysala temples stand on a raised jagati platform of about one metre, and their stellate plan peaked in the twelfth century.

nf1cb74fab4e.s: The Hoysaleswara (Shiva) temple at Halebid was built by:
nf1cb74fab4e.x: Ketamalla, an officer of Vishnuvardhana, built the Hoysaleswara temple (c. 1121); Vishnuvardhana himself built the Chennakeshava at Belur (1117).

ndf53204aeb1.s: The Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana (Bittideva) converted from Jainism to Vaishnavism under the influence of:
ndf53204aeb1.x: Bittideva became a Vaishnava under Ramanuja, who had taken refuge from Chola persecution; his queen Shantala Devi remained a Jain.

nindian-history-149-11.s: Hoysala temples with lathe-turned pillars and star-shaped plans were built of soft:
nindian-history-149-11.x: Hoysala temples used soft chlorite schist (soapstone), had stellate plans and lathe-turned pillars, and were richly carved.

n30d60d931f0.s: In which year did Malik Kafur take the Hoysala capital Dwarasamudra?
n30d60d931f0.x: Malik Kafur took Dwarasamudra in 1311 in a campaign affecting the Yadavas, Kakatiyas, Hoysalas and Pandyas.

nba841991614.s: The Keshava temple at Somanathapura (1268) was built by Somanatha, the general of:
nba841991614.x: The Vishnu (Keshava) temple at Somanathapura was built in 1268 by Somanatha, general of Narasimha III.

n08f3a741f8a.s: Which of the following pairs (Delhi Sultanate and the Yadavas) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Raid of 1295 – Alauddin Khalji, acting for Sultan Jalaluddin
Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18 – Harapaladeva killed
Malik Kafur's campaign of 1307-08 – submission of Harapaladeva
Charge of conquered Andhra after 1323 – Malik Burhanuddin
n08f3a741f8a.x: In 1307-08 it was Ramachandra who submitted and was taken to Delhi; Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18.

nd6f5aedd56e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: too few dates given)
nd6f5aedd56e.s: Which Yadava ruler threw off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship and founded Devagiri as the capital?
nd6f5aedd56e.x: Bhillama V founded Devagiri (c. 1187) after throwing off Kalyani Chalukya overlordship; the Seuna Yadavas' mother tongue was Marathi.

nb43f49add06.s: The school at Patan for teaching Bhaskaracharya's works was established by:
nb43f49add06.x: Changadeva, an astronomer and grandson of Bhaskaracharya, established the school at Patan; Sarngadeva was associated with music.

n976b62bfe1d.s: Sarangapanideva, who later served at Rudramadevi's court, was the son of which Yadava ruler?
n976b62bfe1d.x: Singhana II's son Sarangapanideva served at Rudramadevi's court.

n78d315f757c.s: Hemadpanti architecture, using local black basalt with dressed stones interlocked without mortar, is described as:
n78d315f757c.x: Hemadpanti buildings interlocked dressed black basalt stones without mortar, a technique known as dry masonry.

na6213e663c8.s: Which Yadava ruler killed the Kakatiya Rudradeva and later released Ganapatideva in 1199?
na6213e663c8.x: Jaitugi killed Rudradeva, held Ganapatideva captive, released him in 1199 and married his daughter Somaladevi to him.

n120053f3681.s: The Sangita Ratnakara, a basic text of both Hindustani and Carnatic music, was written by:
n120053f3681.x: Sarngadeva, the court musician of Singhana II, wrote the Sangita Ratnakara.

nb23686dbe37.s: The Dnyaneshwari, written in 1290 at Nevasa, is a Marathi commentary on the:
nb23686dbe37.x: The Dnyaneshwari is a Marathi commentary on the Gita, written in 1290 at Nevasa in the reign of Ramachandra.

n8b3fe927df0.s: The last Yadava ruler Harapaladeva was killed during the invasion of:
n8b3fe927df0.x: Harapaladeva was killed in Mubarak Khalji's invasion of 1317-18; Shankaradeva died during Malik Kafur's invasion in 1313.

n404db0ecfd7.s: In which year was the Yadava ruler Shankaradeva killed?
n404db0ecfd7.x: The sequence was the first invasion in 1295, Malik Kafur's campaign in 1307-08, Shankaradeva's death in 1313 and Harapaladeva's death in 1317-18.

nd7046ab421d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Thousand Pillar inscription?
o: It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
It records the Kakatiya declaration of independence.
nd7046ab421d.x: The Thousand Pillar (Anumakonda) inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva, not Ganapatideva.

n06739f0efb5.s: Which of the following Kakatiya pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Mahadeva – construction of the Ramappa temple
Durgaraja – donations to the Betesvara temple
Prola II – victory pillar at Srisailam
n06739f0efb5.x: The Ramappa temple belongs to Ganapatideva's reign, not Mahadeva's; the other pairs are correct.

n6a5bc86de71.s: The early Kakatiyas were followers of Jainism who later became:
n6a5bc86de71.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains who later became Shaivas (APPSC G2 2011); their sovereign phase ran from 1163 to 1323.

n3ea0643bdfc.s: The Kakatiya general Recherla Rudra bore the title:
n3ea0643bdfc.x: Recherla Rudra was Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya; Prasadaditya was Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya.

n9468177aa18.s: In which year did Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore kill Prithviswara, ending the Velanati kingdom?
n9468177aa18.x: Prithviswara was killed in 1210, ending the Velanati kingdom, and both rulers took the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.

nced6cdf9c2d.s: After the conquest of 1323, the Kakatiya capital Orugallu was renamed:
nced6cdf9c2d.x: Orugallu was renamed Sultanpur after 1323; Andhranagari was a name used under Ganapatideva.

n3b3ad3aff04.s: Ganapatideva restored which ruler to the Nellore throne after the poet Tikkana came to him as envoy?
n3b3ad3aff04.x: Ganapatideva restored Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne; Tikkana went to him as envoy.

ne10137169b2.s: The Kakatiya inscription referring to the Ramappa temple is the one at:
ne10137169b2.x: The Palampet inscription refers to the Ramappa temple; Sanigaram refers to Juddha Mallajinalaya, Dharmasagara to Jalakaranda and Pithapuram to Kolleru Lake.

nindian-history-150-20.s: Which Kakatiya ruler was also called Prataparudra I?
nindian-history-150-20.x: Rudradeva was also called Prataparudra I; Mahadeva came after him, and Ganapatideva was Rudrama Devi's father.

ncde45919207.s: 'Andhra Deshadhiswara' was the title of which Kakatiya ruler?
ncde45919207.x: Andhra Deshadhiswara was Ganapatideva's title; Chola Chamuvardhi was Beta I's, Vikrama Chakri Beta II's and Vinaya Vibhushanudu Rudradeva's.

n918b40913a9.s: Rudrama Devi's training as successor to Ganapatideva was guided by her mother:
n918b40913a9.x: Her mother Kupama Devi guided her training; Mailamba was Ganapatideva's sister. Rudrama Devi ruled 1262-1289.

n2ed9138dd68.s: Which commander of Prataparudra defeated the Hoysala Ballala III after 1316?
n2ed9138dd68.x: Prataparudra's commander Pedarudru defeated Ballala III after 1316; earlier, Veera Ballala II's advance had led Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.

nindian-history-149-2-17.s: Which of the following powers was NOT defeated by Rudrama Devi?
nindian-history-149-2-17.x: Rudrama Devi defeated the Pandyas, the Eastern Gangas and the Seunas of Devagiri; the Western Chalukyas had declined long before her reign.

n9c7074ad2b4.s: In 1257, Ganapatideva, allied with Akkana and Bayyana, killed which ruler, finally ending the Velanati Chodas?
n9c7074ad2b4.x: The 1257 alliance killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola, the final end of the Velanati Chodas; Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi, not Ganapatideva.

n3ab291b82d1.s: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions from the reign of:
n3ab291b82d1.x: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions from Ganapatideva's reign, not Rudradeva's.

n12189b782ea.s: The first inscription of Ganapatideva (26 December 1199) is found at:
n12189b782ea.x: Released from Yadava captivity in 1199, Ganapatideva issued his first inscription at Manthena; he later bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara.

n0fdd843157a.s: The early territorial base of the Kakatiyas was the:
n0fdd843157a.x: The early Kakatiya base was Hanamkonda Vishaya (modern Karimnagar, Warangal, Khammam); they served the Rashtrakutas first and then the Kalyani Chalukyas.

n9aa20f69335.s: The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas (Sevunas) of Devagiri began in the reign of:
n9aa20f69335.x: The Yadava conflict began under Prola II, who was killed by the Velanati Chodas; Rudradeva defeated the Kalachuri confederacy in 1159.

nap-history-6-22.s: In which year was the Rudreshwara (Thousand Pillar) Temple built by Rudradeva?
nap-history-6-22.x: The Rudreswara (Thousand Pillar) Temple is a Kakatiya temple built in 1163 CE by Rudradeva, also called Prataparudra I.

nap-history-3-25.s: The Kazipet inscription records the accession to the throne of:
nap-history-3-25.x: The Kazipet inscription, associated with Betha Raju II (Durgaraja), records Durga Nripathi coming to the throne.

ndf9a33a9cf9.s: Which Kakatiya ruler reigned from 1158 to 1195?
ndf9a33a9cf9.x: Rudradeva ruled 1158-1195, after Beta II (1076-1108) and Prola II (1116-1157), and before Mahadeva (1195-1199).

n792c3c67dac.s: Which Kakatiya ruler completed the city of Orugallu and fully moved the court there?
n792c3c67dac.x: Rudradeva shifted the capital and began fortifying Orugallu; Ganapatideva completed the city and fully transferred the court there.

n9e2d3cf0466.s: One tradition names the progenitor of the Kakatiyas as Kakara Gundana of:
n9e2d3cf0466.x: The progenitor is identified either as Kakara Gundana of Magallu or as Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram.

nc90e0516e9f.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 was issued by which Kakatiya ruler?
nc90e0516e9f.x: Ganapatideva, who ruled 63 years, issued the Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam in 1244; the Ramappa temple was built in his reign by Recherla Rudra.

ncbec8be23c7.s: After the Battle of Muttukur (1263), Nellore fell to the:
ncbec8be23c7.x: The Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva at Muttukur in 1263, and Nellore fell to them.

n2fa3961b40c.s: The Magallu grant of 956, containing the first mention of the Kakatiya family, was issued by the Eastern Chalukya ruler:
n2fa3961b40c.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava (956) first mentions the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.

n3f94f23780f.s: The title 'Kumara Rudradeva' was borne at his accession by:
n3f94f23780f.x: Kumara Rudradeva was the title borne by Prataparudra II at his accession.

n5fa002729ae.s: In which year was the Ramappa Temple at Palampet inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
n5fa002729ae.x: The Ramappa Temple, noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021.

n57362b54795.s: After the Tughlaq conquest of Orugallu in 1323, who was placed in charge of Andhra?
n57362b54795.x: After the 1321-22 and 1323 invasions, Orugallu was renamed Sultanpur and Malik Burhanuddin was placed in charge of Andhra.

nbbedc87ad8a.s: According to the Vilasa copper plate, the captured Prataparudra drowned himself in the river:
nbbedc87ad8a.x: Prataparudra surrendered in 1323 and, while being taken towards Delhi, drowned himself; the Vilasa record names the Narmada (another account names the Kaveri).

n7af0c68d0d8.s: In 1311, Prataparudra's forces joined Malik Kafur's march on Madurai under the command of:
n7af0c68d0d8.x: Prataparudra's forces under Muppidi Nayaka joined Malik Kafur's march on Madurai in 1311; after Alauddin's death in 1316 he stopped paying tribute.

ne669af0e0bc.s: In which year did Rudrama Devi begin ruling as Rudradeva Maharaja under co-regency with Ganapatideva?
ne669af0e0bc.x: Rudrama began co-regency in 1258; the 1266 Tripurantakam inscription still called her a vassal, and she was fully crowned after Ganapatideva's death in 1262.

n5fbae372409.s: During Prataparudra's campaigns, Ranganatha of Nellore, a Pandya ally, was replaced by:
n5fbae372409.x: Ranganatha of Nellore was replaced by Manuma Gandapalu; Ambadeva's principality was annexed and Gonavithala pushed towards Devagiri.

n445269adcc8.s: Rudrama Devi was killed in 1289 while fighting the rebel:
n445269adcc8.x: She died in 1289 fighting Kayastha Ambadeva, with Mallikarjuna Nayaka as her general; her servant Puvvula Mummadi set up the Chandupatla inscription.

nd66e92f2a1d.s: Prataparudra II, crowned in 1289, was Rudrama Devi's grandson through her daughter:
nd66e92f2a1d.x: Prataparudra II was Rudrama Devi's grandson through Mummadamma; she trained him and he was crowned in 1289.

nap-history-29-11.x: Kumaragiri Reddy succeeded Anavema Reddy; among the Kakatiyas, Rudra Deva came after Prola Raju II and Mahadeva succeeded Rudra Deva.

n4b01a725e68.s: Vengi, occupied by Ganga Narasimhadeva in 1262, was recovered by the Kakatiyas in:
n4b01a725e68.x: Vengi was recovered in 1278 after Poti Nayaka and Prolinayaka defeated Virabhanudeva.

n39cf31da630.s: Rudrama Devi, daughter of Ganapatideva, was married to the Chalukya prince:
n39cf31da630.x: Rudrama Devi married the Chalukya prince Veerabhadra; her daughter Rudramma married the Yadava prince Ellanadeva.

n93ccf5100f3.s: The second Khalji invasion of Warangal (1309-10) was led by:
n93ccf5100f3.x: Malik Kafur led the 1309-10 invasion; Prataparudra submitted, paid a large tribute and accepted Delhi's overlordship.

nbed73ba39d5.s: Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing Malik Kafur's 1310 siege of Warangal, was written by:
nbed73ba39d5.x: Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh, describing the double-walled Warangal fort with a moat; he called Prataparudra 'Ravaddar Dev'.

n595f1383ddd.s: Madhura Vijayam, which describes the hardship following the conquest of the Kakatiya kingdom, was written by:
n595f1383ddd.x: Gangadevi's Madhura Vijayam and the Vilasa grant of Prolaya Nayaka describe the hardship after the conquest.

nd50979f44be.s: According to Marco Polo, the local grain of the Kakatiya realm was:
nd50979f44be.x: Marco Polo noted rice as the local grain, along with sea trade, fine textiles and diamonds, and said merchants were not oppressively taxed.

n1b6a7f1923a.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: too few dates given)
n1b6a7f1923a.s: The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 belonged to the reign of:
n1b6a7f1923a.x: The 1416 Motupalli Dharma Sasanam belonged to Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I; Ganapatideva's Abhaya Sasanam dates to 1244 CE.

n3732fd84682.s: In Kakatiya tank irrigation, linked chain tanks were called:
n3732fd84682.x: Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks passing surplus water downhill; Samudrams were large tanks and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for tank upkeep.

n4c325d1936a.s: Ganapatideva's Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam guaranteed safety to:
n4c325d1936a.x: The charter protected foreign merchants, remitted arbitrary taxes, promised compensation for shipwreck or theft and stopped harassment by officials.

n5859bf05bd7.s: In the Kakatiya period, the head of a merchant guild was called:
n5859bf05bd7.x: The guild head was Setti or Sreshthi; a merchant was a Behari and trade was Vyavaharam.

n32884c33752.s: Under the Vijayanagara Amara-Nayankara system, the land assigned to a nayaka was called:
n32884c33752.x: The land was Amaram and the tribute was Kappam or Kist; the break-up of the system produced the Poligars.

n08c0319e003.s: Who described the Kakatiya state as a 'metropolitan state'?
n08c0319e003.x: Romila Thapar used 'metropolitan state', while Burton Stein's label was 'segmentary state' - two different interpretations.

nap-history-13-2.s: In the Kakatiya revenue system, 'Pullari' was a tax levied on:
nap-history-13-2.x: Pullari was the grazing tax on grass; Putti was the dry-land cess, Ayagarlu held tax-free land and Arigapulu were tax-paying farmers.

n7227af66044.s: According to one account, how many Nayankaras were there in the Kakatiya kingdom?
n7227af66044.x: One account gives 72 Nayankaras, each guarding a fort; together they controlled one-fourth of the kingdom's land.

n51513d4d43b.s: Which of the following crops was NOT grown in the Kakatiya period?
n51513d4d43b.x: Maize reached India only after 1500; betel, rice, sugarcane and cotton were among Kakatiya crops.

ne08410c6cef.x: Pellipannu was the wedding tax; Angadi Sunkam was the weekly-market tax, Dari Sunkam a road toll and Kanika a customary gift.

ne9ee35aac7f.s: In the Kakatiya village, the Talari was the:
ne9ee35aac7f.x: The Talari was the village watchman; the Karanam was the accountant and tolls were collected by the Sunkadhikari/Sunkamanya.

nfda6dcc9b94.s: In Kakatiya central administration, the Kayasthas were:
nfda6dcc9b94.x: The Kayasthas were scribes (APPSC 2012); the Pradvivaka advised the king on the judicial system.

nf0ef6194908.s: In the Kakatiya period, 'Chitrameli' was a samaya (occupational group) of:
nf0ef6194908.x: Samayas were caste or occupational groups, and Chitrameli was the samaya of agricultural farmers (APPSC G2 2019).

nfa630832aca.s: In the Kakatiya period, Nirmal was famous for:
nfa630832aca.x: Knives were associated with Nirmal, ratna kambalu with Warangal and diamonds with the Golconda region; iron came from Guthikonda and Palnadu.

nec63f34ea8f.s: The Pakhala tank of the Kakatiya period was built by:
nec63f34ea8f.x: Mummadi Nayaka built the Pakhala tank; Prola II built Arikesari Samudram, Recherla Rudra the Ramappa tank and Ganapatideva Laknavaram.

nc654ddc4e2c.s: The Pratapa Charitra, a source for the Nayankara system, was written by:
nc654ddc4e2c.x: Ekamranatha wrote the Pratapa Charitra and Baddena the Neeti Sastra Muktavali, both sources on the Nayankara system; Shivadevayya's Purushartha Saram informs on the 72 Niyogas.

n25911d774fe.s: The Motupalli charter is regarded as the most important ____ document of the Kakatiya period.
n25911d774fe.x: The Motupalli charter is called the most important commercial document of the period, showing the state's stake in sea trade.

n9a8215e8f4c.s: According to the Palnati Veeracharitra, Orugallu had about how many painters' houses?
n9a8215e8f4c.x: The Palnati Veeracharitra mentions about 1,500 painters' houses in Orugallu; Machaladevi was a woman painter of the time.

n2cb1694243a.s: Tank-building was one of the Sapta Santanalu, which were the seven:
n2cb1694243a.x: The Sapta Santanalu were seven meritorious acts: son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.

nb5fddaa7cc0.s: Who was the prime minister of the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva?
nb5fddaa7cc0.x: Malyala Hemadri Reddi was Ganapatideva's prime minister; Muppidi Nayudu was prime minister under Prataparudra.

n04e825dcfb0.s: Under the Kakatiya Nayankara system, villages given to Nayakas instead of a salary were called:
n04e825dcfb0.x: Nayakas received Nayakasthalam villages in lieu of salary, maintained a fixed army for the king, paid a fixed annual sum and remitted the rest.

n606715fe223.s: Which Vijayanagara ruler totally withdrew the marriage tax?
n606715fe223.x: Krishnadevaraya withdrew the marriage tax; Moturpha, a British-era tax on trades and looms, was abolished in 1861.

n9c7b18a8904.s: In the Kakatiya army, 'Mula Balam' was:
o: the contingents maintained by the Nayakas
the four arms of the army
n9c7b18a8904.x: Mula Balam was the king's own standing army; the Nayakas' contingents formed the separate Nayankara army and chaturanga bala meant the four arms.

n2e88f90a900.s: Under the Kakatiyas, ports that collected import and export duties were called:
n2e88f90a900.x: Kara Pattanam were ports collecting duties; Krishnapatnam was on the Nellore coast and Hamsaladeevi in the Krishna delta.

n031388c7bec.s: Which of the following was imported, rather than exported, in Kakatiya trade?
n031388c7bec.x: Arabian war horses were imported for the cavalry; textiles, spices, diamonds and gold were exported.

n29eaa9329e8.s: Kakatiya land revenue (Ari or bhaga) was generally what share of the produce?
n29eaa9329e8.x: Land revenue was generally one-sixth of the produce; Koru was the cess on wet (Magani) land and Putti on dry land.

n16564b8e449.s: In Kakatiya military terminology, a 'Giridurga' was a:
n16564b8e449.x: Giridurga was a hill fort (Jaladurga water, Vanadurga forest, Sthaladurga plain); the Warangal fort had concentric walls and a moat.

nindian-history-26-17.s: Sandal, camphor, rose-water and ivory appear among the goods traded at which Kakatiya port?
nindian-history-26-17.x: Sandal, camphor, rose-water and ivory all appear among the goods traded at Motupalli.

n2e177d5a6d8.s: Who called the Kakatiya period the 'Golden Age of the Shudras'?
n2e177d5a6d8.x: Under the Kakatiyas religion and politics became non-Brahmin, and Cynthia Talbot called the period the 'Golden Age of the Shudras'.

n3dc4632f1ea.s: The Kakatiya Ayagar system of village administration consisted of how many functionaries?
n3dc4632f1ea.x: The Ayagars were twelve village functionaries (APPSC G2 2012), paid by shares of produce and service lands.
